decisions.reason: The whitespace feedback lists changing the font only as an uncertain possible remedy. The separate font clause already establishes Garamond and its readability constraint, so the whitespace decision necessitates no additional typography change.
Eliminating visible whitespace at article ends does not change the table-of-contents completion timing or finalized-page-number accuracy rules.
The possible use of more advertisements to fill whitespace does not alter the independent requirement that advertisements render sharply rather than blur.
The article-end whitespace policy does not change the rule that cover article page numbers must be accurate.
Article-end whitespace balance is distinct from maintaining compatibility and balance across flipbook two-page spreads.
The whitespace decision does not change where red may be used.
The new atomic article-end whitespace constraint does not modify the existing polished, modern, brand-aligned visual-style attributes.
The whitespace policy adds an article-page presentation constraint but does not change the magazine's template obligation, supplied inputs, compilation action, or Flat Plan arrangement basis.
The whitespace decision does not alter which cover-listed articles must be included or who chooses their placement.
Images are mentioned only as one uncertain way to fill whitespace. The decision does not change the existing requirement to use AI when necessary to improve article-image quality.
The article-end whitespace policy does not change the specified source of article content.
The whitespace decision does not change article category requirements, category sources, allowed categories, or label presentation.
